name: markdown-links-deferred
body:
Markdown links are DEFERRED — out of scope for the scanner-optimisation change-set (Human decision). The markdown frontend scans documents as File nodes with heading Struct sections; turning links between documents/sections into Uses/UnresolvedUse edges is a FUTURE feature. Reason: scope — links are a distinct capability (path-base resolution rules, source/target anchoring, cross-document resolution context) while this project's core is the scan/cache/assemble optimisation; the markdown frontend itself (documents -> File + heading section symbols) is in scope, links are not.

Consequences of the deferral:
- The synthesized document-root section Struct existed ONLY to give a whole-document/preamble link a representable Struct source/target (a File is not a legal Uses endpoint under the graph schema). With links out of scope it is retired too: a heading-less document now yields only its File node, no section Structs, and the sections of a document are exactly its headings.
- The link-exactness requirement (never-guess for links) is retired with the feature.
- The retired requirements are requirements.requirement.markdown-links-as-edges and requirements.requirement.markdown-exactness-unresolved; their nodes and every incident edge were removed cleanly (no orphan, no dangling half).

When links land they will reintroduce an anchoring decision (likely re-adding a document-root Struct, or an equivalent representable source/target) as a NEW requirement in a later change-set. This note records the deferral so the retirement is not read as an oversight.
